perspective.description: Busy partner/family carer without a persistent access impairment, often interrupted; wants practical support while respecting the person's choices. Values printable questions, communication preferences and clear privacy boundaries; dislikes long reading lists before useful actions, patronising instructions and pressure to disclose another person's details.

navigation.deduction: None; all menu destinations, direct routes, history and legacy routes worked.

readingAccess.deduction: Doubled app text at 320px pushed the title below the first viewport; true browser zoom and screen-reader support were not tested.

practicalUsefulness.deduction: None; practical question, preference, guide and card flows were usable with invented values.

dataOutputTrust.deduction: Medical-card PDF had a date-only second page; no-event-date medical card still showed an update date.

recoveryFromInterruption.deduction: In-session return and explicit saves worked, but unsaved sheet reload cleared data and native confirmation results were partly uninspectable.

verdict: Useful, practical support flows are easy to reach and respect optional disclosure. Improve the narrow doubled-text layout and medical-card print output/date clarity; confirmation and native print behavior remain partly untested.
firstUse: Home exposed practical actions without requiring a long reading sequence. Review-pending and development-preview status were visible. A carer could build useful questions and communication preferences without entering real identity or contact details.
strengths: Practical tools were easy to reach from Home.
Question and communication-preference sheets supported select, remove, note, preview, return and explicit save.
Optional invented card values were sufficient; real phone numbers or another person's details were unnecessary.
Local-save/privacy statements and generic saved-item labels clarified device storage.
Guide review status, sources, limitations, simplified/one-section modes and manual speech controls were visible.
Actual TXT, PDF and milestone PNG exports were inspected; milestone no-event-date outputs were consistent.
frustrations: At 200% app text in 320px, the header took many lines and pushed the title below the first viewport.
Medical-card PDF page two held only the update date and footer.
A medical card with no event date still displayed an update date that could be confused with one without clear labeling.
Unsaved sheet content survived in-session navigation but not reload.
Print status did not expose an inspectable print surface in the IAB.

findings.title: Doubled app text pushes Home title below first view at 320px
findings.expected: Practical entry point remains reasonably quick to reach.
findings.actual: Header wraps across many lines and title begins below initial viewport. documentElement.scrollWidth remains 320px; no horizontal overflow or proven clipping.

findings.title: Medical-card PDF creates a date-only second page
steps: Fill optional medical-card fields with synthetic values
findings.expected: Printable card occupies a compact page with its related information.
findings.actual: Page one contains the card; page two contains only Last updated 2026-10-13 and a footer.

findings.title: No event date still displays an update date
steps: Create and save a medical card
Choose No date for the event date
Inspect preview and actual TXT/PDF exports
findings.expected: The event-date choice is unambiguous and separate from any update timestamp.
findings.actual: No event date is selected, while preview, TXT and PDF contain Last updated 2026-10-13. This is an update date, not a false event date, but needs a clear label.

findings.title: Native delete/cancel and clear-all confirmation paths not fully inspectable
steps: Native confirmation was not exposed via supported dialog API; do not repeat timeout-prone dialogs
Support deletion and clear-all result likewise unavailable
findings.expected: Both confirm and cancel outcomes can be observed and verified.
findings.actual: Appointment later displayed Saved sheet deleted from this app's device storage; its cancel path was not tested. Support delete and clear-all outcomes could not be reliably inspected. No repeated action was attempted.

findings.title: Native print layout not exposed in IAB
findings.expected: Print layout and cancel state can be inspected.
findings.actual: App status said print view opened and to choose Print or Cancel, but no inspectable preview surface or browser cancellation control was available.

limits: Simulated UX/engineering review; not patient/carer feedback or clinical/accessibility approval.
True browser zoom, NVDA/screen reader, native devices and audible speech were not tested.
Privacy request inspection was limited to one synthetic save/reload session.
No physical print, external upload, Facebook, login or patient-specific AI timing workflow was used.
Temporary viewport/display settings were reset; only T4 tabs were closed before browser release.
